name: Telecom Tower (Ufone Tower)
assumptions: Reading the OSM footprint and the south-west elevation photo as one building of two wings joined by a connector; every level was scaled off that one photo at about 13.5 px per metre.

113 m is taken as the rear glass ridge; allowing for the ridge standing 34 m further from the camera, all south-west elevation levels were scaled by 0.95, which puts the wedge tip near 100.7 m. Near-camera photos make the wedge look highest, and sources do not say which part the 113 m means.
Floor pitch 4.0 m from the photo gives 12 front and 18 rear fascia bands; sources disagree on the total floor count (20, 24, 28).
The wedge roof is a single plane rising to the south-west edge, inferred from the front view and the level top seen from the south-west.
The circular window is sized from the photo as 0.22 of the 26 m front face, so about 5.9 m; the dossier's 7.5 m assumed a wider face.
North-east face of the rear wing mirrors the south-west face; no photo shows it.
Rear glass roof pitch and the panel widths are read from two distant photos.
Podium outline beyond the OSM footprint (about 7.5 m forward and sideways with a rounded corner, and a colonnade block about 10 m past the rear wing) is estimated from photos; depth is unknown.
The exterior lift strip on the north-east flank follows the dossier; its top (63 m) and width are estimates from one distant photo.
White strips, orange sweep and big ufone signs are the advertising wrap of the most recent photos, and it changes over the years.
Glass mullion spacing and the louvre count on the north-west end are representative, not counted exactly.
Night lighting colours follow the two night photos; the rest of the night look is estimated.
